FEASIBILITY PROTOTYPE for your canonical-order decision, measured before Epic 5 builds the accumulator. Your decision is achievable, and cheaply.

Setup: n = 200 observations, p = 60 features, residual cross-products accumulated under five different workspace block plans (5, 7, 12, 20, 60 columns). Bitwise identity across plans is the target.

  A  naive crossprod per block pair          bitwise identical: NO   max|diff| = 1.42e-13   0.003s
  B  fixed canonical tile shape (pad to 64)  bitwise identical: YES  max|diff| = 0          0.006s
  C  per-pair dot, fixed element order       bitwise identical: YES  max|diff| = 0          0.082s

Strategy B costs 2x naive. Strategy C costs 27x. Recommend B.

The mechanism, which is the useful part

The nondeterminism is not accumulation order in your code - it is BLAS selecting different kernels, blocking and vectorization for different MATRIX SHAPES. Strategy A feeds a differently shaped GEMM for every block plan, so the reduction tree inside BLAS changes. Fix the shape and the result is reproducible regardless of how much memory you gave the workspace.

Design consequence for Epic 5: DECOUPLE THE CANONICAL TILE SHAPE FROM THE MEMORY BUDGET. The budget should control how many tiles are in flight, never the dimensions of the GEMM. That is the single rule that makes the guarantee hold.

Refinement worth taking: padding every support to one width wastes flops when supports are small (padding a 5-column block to 64 does ~13x the useful work in that GEMM). Since your supports have a known size distribution from the Epic 1 cost report, bucket them into a small fixed set of canonical widths - powers of two over the observed support range - so every GEMM shape is drawn from a fixed set. Determinism holds because the shape set is fixed and plan-independent, and padding waste stays bounded because each support goes to the next bucket rather than to the global maximum.

Note strategy C also differs from a single-shot crossprod(R) by 5.7e-14. That is expected and harmless - a fixed element order is simply a different summation order than BLAS uses. The guarantee you want is self-consistency across block plans, not agreement with an unblocked BLAS call, so B is the right target and it delivers exactly that.
